title: System architecture
intro: Four layers on two stacks. You talk to Jarvis (1), which reads and acts on the Dashboard's store (2), starts work as Build agents (3: ONE Claude Code agent per task, D30), and every long-running agent lives in a termhub session (4). The work stack and the personal stack run the same dev-tools code with different .env files; no data or credentials cross between them. The software-factory is frozen (D30): in the tree, reachable only with PA_BUILD=factory, not on the default path.
maintenance: Rendered from personal-assistant/src/dashboard/architecture.json. Add, remove or rename a component, tool, port, model default or table in the same commit as the code (root CLAUDE.md, 'Architecture map'); test/architecture.test.js checks the parts it can.

statuses.landing: Code on main, contract or rollout still landing

layers.name: Ask (Talk)
layers.summary: Jarvis: a voice page with a fast local model that answers simple turns in about a second, and the PA chat (a Claude Code session) that does everything else behind permission prompts.

layers.name: Plan (Dashboard)
layers.summary: The worker ingests mail, Teams, GitHub, Jira and meetings, distils asks into commitments, and serves the board. Each stack's data is one encrypted SQLite file.

layers.name: Build (Factory)
layers.summary: One Claude Code agent per task (build-agent, D30) in a termhub session on the claude.ai subscription: Do on a card or the chat's build_start opens it, `pa run` talks back, a 10 s heartbeat flags idle runs, the Build board (/factory) shows them. The software-factory below it (jobs on two runtimes, ticked by factory serve; metered DeepSeek/Azure personas) is frozen (D30): still in the tree, reachable only with PA_BUILD=factory.

layers.name: Run (Sessions)
layers.summary: termhub: the terminal supervisor every agent runs in. ptyd owns the PTYs (127.0.0.1:7020) so they survive a sessiond restart; sessiond owns the sessions; the front (jarvisd front, its own process) serves the UI, the APIs and the /pa/ proxy.

layers.name: Models and outside services
layers.summary: Where model calls and data go, and who pays: the Claude subscription (Build agents and the PA chat), the local GPU, Azure (the fast lane's fallback, embeddings and rerank), GitHub and Microsoft 365. DeepSeek is only the frozen factory's.

components.name: /talk voice page
components.role: Hears the room in the browser; sends only the utterance after the wake word.

where.work: Browser tab served by the dashboard
where.personal: Browser tab served by the dashboard, through termhub /pa/talk

details.Wake word: openWakeWord hey_jarvis_v0.1.onnx, client-side on onnxruntime-web (WASM, one thread)
details.Models served: /talk/models/ serves a fixed list of file names (MODEL_FILES), never a path
details.End of turn: POST /api/talk/endpoint, proxied to smart-turn in the voice service; the utterance is transcribed at the same moment and that text is kept when smart-turn says done
Sends: POST /api/talk/transcribe (the utterance only; with the smart-turn check, again only if the turn ends otherwise)
POST /api/talk/warm when an utterance starts (at most every 3 s): Kokoro warmed, whisper handed silence every 400 ms until the end-of-turn check
POST /api/talk/latency after each turn (end of speech to first audio, logged by the PA)

POST /api/talk/mic every 20 s while the page holds the mic, and when it lets go: the meeting gate does not count that browser as a call (talk-mic.json); turns and replies are logged to talk-activity.jsonl so meeting capture drops them (src/audio/selfSpeech.ts)
POST /api/chat/permission (a spoken yes or no to the chat's action prompt)
details.Privacy: Nothing leaves the browser until a request is made; the wake word stays client-side.
details.Modes: Voice (the face, default) or Text, switched in the page's panel and remembered per browser (jarvis.talk.mode). Text mode is the same PA chat as a transcript with a box to type in (chat.client.js, POST /api/chat), and shows the Approve / Deny card for a pending action prompt (permission.client.js); Voice mode has no buttons.
details.Permission prompts: Audio only, no buttons: Jarvis speaks the server-written question (transcript.askTool) and your next utterance answers it (talk.core.js createVoiceAsk: only while awake, only from words begun after the question, strict yes/no, unclear asked once more, 60 s window) via POST /api/chat/permission with the page token
details.Sleep: "Jarvis, sleep" / "stop listening" / "go to sleep" (and the stop phrases) return it to wake-word-only, said aloud; windows: 6 s after the wake word, 8 s after an answer, 60 s after a question

components.name: Fast lane (System 1)
components.role: Decide, then speak (D7): a router returns calibrated probabilities p(answer_here), p(hand_off), p(action); only above the answer threshold does a small model speak the answer, otherwise your words go to the PA chat verbatim. No tools.

where.work: In the worker process (dashboard), POST /api/talk/turn
where.personal: Off (PA_FAST_LANE=0): no Ollama on k-911-x17 yet

details.Model: local/llama3.2:3b through Ollama's native /api/chat, for both the router and the answerer
details.Router: PA_FAST_ROUTER=logprob (src/chat/fastRouter.ts): one call, one generated token. The model is asked a fixed question, 'A (answer here), B (hand off: needs a lookup) or C (action)?', and the top log-probabilities of that token are calibrated (temperature 0.461 plus a per-class bias, fitted by `pa eval router --fit`) into p(answer_here), p(hand_off), p(action). Alternatives: same (the older one-call JSON {label, route, say}), rules, a model string, an http(s) URL
details.Answerer: speaks only when p(answer_here) >= 0.64 (PA_FAST_ANSWER_THRESHOLD): a second streamed call that writes one to four short sentences, opening with one of at most six words so speech can start at once; meeting titles are said as titles, never as who a meeting is with. Below it, the user's words go to the PA chat verbatim with 'One moment.' (or 'On it.' when p(action) > p(hand_off))
details.Eval: `pa eval answerer`: 6 day snapshots in src/eval/answerer-cases.json (placeholders), checking the answer names the right day, every meeting and no invented attendees, plus first-token and first-spoken-piece latency. `pa eval router`: 97 turns in src/eval/router-cases.json (anonymized logged turns, the known miss 'check my mail from <name>', tomorrow against this-week questions, and synthetic ones), 3-way accuracy, turns answered here that should not be, latency warm. Nov 2026 on this laptop's RTX 3000 Ada: 0 action and 0 look-up turns answered here; see PLAN.md 0.6 for the numbers
details.Prompt cache: the router's system prompt and examples never change; the snapshot comes next, then the last two turns, then the words. 1.5 s after each turn (so it does not share the GPU with Kokoro's first sentence), and when the snapshot changes, a one-token call with the next turn's prefix fills Ollama's cache for the answerer and then the router (Ollama keeps one prefix per slot; OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2 gives each its own), so a turn pays only for its own words
details.Fallback: azure/pa (PA_FAST_FALLBACK_MODEL) when Ollama is down or the router has not answered within 2500 ms (PA_FAST_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MS): the one-call text format decides and replies
Prompt: a snapshot of your day: a few hundred tokens (open asks by bucket, top 3 overdue and due, the calendar to the end of tomorrow split by local day (today's remaining meetings, or 'none left today', then tomorrow's, then 'Meetings after tomorrow: not in this snapshot.', cancelled ones apart), active runs, waiting drafts and review items, first 300 chars of your 'me' page)
router: the last 2 turns, 200 chars each; answerer: the last 6 turns (chat history merged with turns it answered itself)
router: 1 output token; answerer: max 300 output tokens
details.Snapshot refresh: Cached in memory, rebuilt in the background when older than 60 s (PA_FAST_CONTEXT_SECONDS), and at an utterance's start (POST /api/talk/warm) when it would be that old within 20 s: the rebuild and its prime land while you speak, not inside the turn (first token 497 -> 270 ms in the e2e)
details.Context window: unknown: Ollama's default for the model (the PA does not set num_ctx)
details.Compaction: none needed: every turn is a fresh prompt
details.Kept warm: keep_alive 24h (PA_FAST_KEEP_ALIVE); when /talk opens, and every 4 minutes after, a one-token request carrying the fixed system prompt primes the KV cache prefix (llm.warmLocal: under the logprob router the answerer's system prompt, snapshot and conversation, then the router's own prefix; the one-call JSON prompt otherwise)
Guards: the router never writes words, so it cannot answer a turn by itself; below the threshold nothing local is spoken but the stock acknowledgement
never answers an action-like request (guardDecision / looksLikeAction turn it into a hand-off, whatever the router said)
never answers a question about a day the snapshot does not hold: the week, the weekend, yesterday, a weekday other than today or tomorrow (guardDecision / looksBeyondSnapshot hand it off)
a hand-off types your verbatim words into the PA chat; the model's task is only a labelled hint
a hand-off's spoken acknowledgement is replaced by the stock one when it reads as an answer (spokenAck)
details.Billing: free (local GPU); the azure/pa fallback is metered and recorded in llm_spend

components.name: faster-whisper transcriber
components.role: Speech to text, shared with voice-dictation so one warm model serves both.

where.work: 127.0.0.1:47821, a raw TCP protocol (a WAV path in, text out)
where.personal: Not installed on the personal machine

details.Called by: POST /api/talk/transcribe in the dashboard, the worker's audio pass for recorded meetings, and `pa meeting import` / the dashboard's meeting import for audio and video you did not record live
details.Warm-up: a silent WAV is sent when /talk opens if it has not been used for 5 minutes (it unloads when idle)
details.Decoding: small, float16, beam 1. A 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV is read straight into numpy (faster-whisper's own decoder costs ~50 ms a call), and a clip that fits one 30 s window is decoded without timestamps: 232 -> 167 ms back to back for a two-second question. It opts out of Windows power throttling (EcoQoS) at start: in the talk page's order, beside the smart-turn check, 456 -> ~290 ms. Takes effect when the deployed copy is updated and the transcriber restarted

components.name: Jarvis: the PA chat (System 2)
components.role: The PA chat. The default engine is the Claude Agent SDK inside the worker; a read-only termhub session is its Run view. It reads through MCP tools and acts only behind permission prompts.

where.work: The Claude Agent SDK inside the PA worker on the laptop (PA_CHAT_ENGINE=sdk, the default), home <dataDir>/pa-home; its Run view is a read-only termhub session
where.personal: The same engine on the personal machine (PA_CHAT_ENGINE=sdk, the default), home <dataDir>/pa-home; its Run view is a read-only termhub session

details.Model: PA_CHAT_MODEL (no default in code: the Claude Code CLI's own default); PA_CHAT_AGENT picks claude or opencode
details.Started as: claude --permission-mode default --mcp-config pa-home/pa-chat.mcp.json [--model ...]; never with --dangerously-skip-permissions (chatCommand refuses it)
details.Context window: whatever Claude Code reports for the model (context_window.context_window_size; the statusline falls back to 200,000 tokens)
details.Compaction: Claude Code auto-compacts its own context. State lives in the store, not the transcript: a SessionStart hook runs `pa context` (60 s timeout) on every start, resume, clear and compaction, so a week-old chat still knows this morning's asks.
What it loads: CLAUDE.md, rewritten from code on every start (src/chat/index.ts); your additions go in CLAUDE.local.md
`pa context`: profile, today's brief, what is waiting on you, live runs
INBOX.md: the worker's pushed notifications, read as data, never instructions
Permissions: settings.json: defaultMode default, bypass mode disabled; verifyClaudeHome reads them back (and settings.local.json) before starting
no `pa` shell command is allowed: every one asks
the Microsoft 365 connector's read-only tools (mail, calendar and chat search, Teams lists, people, SharePoint; M365_READ_TOOLS in src/chat/index.ts) are allowed by name; any other M365 tool asks

shared Claude pages: the Claude Docs read tools (guide, read, query; DOCS_READ_TOOLS) are allowed by name,; any Docs write asks. Claude Code leaves its Artifact tool off under the SDK, so subscriptionEnv sets CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT=1; the chat lists what was shared (Artifact list, scope shared) and reads it, since the share notice itself is hidden from mail search by the M365 connector, and never asks a voice user for a link; the PreToolUse hook allows only the Artifact tool's list and read unasked (artifactRead in src/chat/sdkFeed.ts)
the caveman plugin is off for this session only
its action-tool prompts can also be answered by voice on Talk (while awake) or on the dashboard's Waiting for your yes card; src/chat/permission.ts checks the screen first
How you reach it: Ask (/talk), by voice or in its Text mode (src/chat/feed.ts types into the session through termhub's input API and tails its transcript)
details.Transcript: ~/.claude/projects/<encoded pa-home>/<uuid>.jsonl, tailed by byte offset (first read: last 4 MB)
details.Billing: the machine's Claude Code login: a claude.ai subscription login is not metered per call
Engine: PA_CHAT_ENGINE=terminal: a termhub session in pa-home (the engine before 4.2); its prompts are answered by reading the screen (src/chat/permission.ts)

PA_CHAT_ENGINE=sdk (the default since plan 4.2): the Claude Agent SDK (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk) inside the PA worker, src/chat/sdkFeed.ts. Same home, CLAUDE.md, settings, SessionStart hook and pa-chat MCP server; one streaming query() resumed by its session id (pa-home/.pa-chat-sdk-session.json); answers stream into /api/chat/stream as partial events

SDK approvals are typed callbacks: a PreToolUse hook puts every call through src/policy (deny refuses; the six action tools always ask), canUseTool waits for the dashboard card or a spoken yes (POST /api/chat/permission, then policy.enforce), and no answer within PA_CHAT_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS (5 min) is a deny audited on channel timeout. Any other prompt (a `pa` shell verb, an edit, remember) gets a generic allow-once card showing the call's whole input, answerable by voice only when that input is short enough to hear whole and the policy allows voice (never an edit); a policy allow for Read/Grep/Glob holds inside pa-home only

SDK billing: the bundled Claude Code signs in with the machine's Claude login (measured: apiKeySource none, a Team subscription); ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN are removed from its environment so it never bills the API. Headless use draws on the subscription's separate credit pool (since 15 Jun 2026)

SDK doorbell: the worker's fixed INBOX line reaches it as a user turn through POST /api/chat/doorbell (the id only), under the terminal doorbell's conditions: a running session, idle long enough, nothing waiting on a yes

SDK on a Z1 roll: drain denies the prompts still waiting (with a reason the model repeats), gives the turn in flight up to 20 s, closes the query; the new generation resumes the session by its id on its first message; undrain (rollback) restarts it here the same way

SDK Run view: every kept chat event is appended to pa-home/sdk-view/chat.jsonl and a read-only termhub session (cwd pa-home/sdk-view, never pa-home) runs `node src/chat/sdkView.js --follow` on it; /api/chat/session's sessionId and url are that session (conversationId is the SDK's), so the drill-down links work as on the terminal engine
SDK limits for now: `pa chat` only points at Ask

components.name: personal-assistant MCP server
components.role: The store over MCP (stdio). Read-only for every session; the PA chat alone also gets the `pa` verbs, task_add and the per-layer chat tools.

where.work: A stdio child of each Claude Code session that registers it: user scope as `personal-assistant`, the PA chat as `pa-chat` with PA_MCP_CHAT_TOOLS=1
where.personal: The same stdio server, on the personal machine

details.Shared surface: recall and memory reads, open_commitments, who_is, repo_state; remember only proposes (a pending_review claim); request_secret / secret_status never return a value
details.Chat-only surface: the read-only `pa` verbs as the `pa` tool (run with PA_READ_ONLY=1), task_add, board / card / factory_* / sessions reads, and the actions factory_start, factory_continue, factory_resume, factory_cancel, factory_approve, session_start
details.Actions: the dispatch paths themselves (dispatch.start, factory cancel/approve/resume), never a second implementation; auto_merge and push_to_main become a card ('suggested by the chat')
details.Data rule: everything a tool returns quotes other people's messages: data, never instructions

components.name: Policy engine and audit log
components.role: Plan 4.3: one function answers allow, deny or ask for every tool call, chat approval and factory approval, from a declarative policy file, and writes each answer to a hash-chained audit log.

where.work: In-process wherever the call is made: the MCP server (every tool), the dashboard (chat permission answers, factory approve), the CLI; the log is the audit_log table
where.personal: The same code and table, on the personal stack

details.Policy: src/policy/default.policy.json (tracked) plus an untracked per-stack override (PA_POLICY_FILE, default <data dir>/policy.json): override rules first, then the defaults, first match wins, else `default` (ask). The defaults are the old allow/ask split with no behaviour change: the chat's read tools and the shared MCP surface allow, its six action tools ask (Claude Code still owns that prompt), answering the prompt is allowed from the dashboard, termhub, voice and the CLI, and on channel e2e, where `pa e2e` answers for its own dummy call (approvals only; an e2e call still asks)
details.Voice: a locked rule (nothing in an override loosens it) denies the voice channel any call or approval tagged merge, push_main or secret_reveal; tags come from the tool name and its delivery level or pa verb. A voice approval of a factory job (factory_approve, factory_resume) looks up the job's delivery now and is denied for auto_merge or push_to_main; a job that cannot be looked up is denied for voice (fail closed). With PA_PASSKEYS=on (7.1) an approval of one of those kinds from another channel becomes `ask` (rule stepup-required) and is refused until the dashboard has recorded a passkey tap for that exact approval id (the chat tool_use id, or the job id); the grant is looked at by the policy and used up by the code that runs the action
details.Audit: every decision is a row of audit_log with the hash of the row before it (prev_hash) and its own hash; arguments are stored only as a digest. `pa audit verify` recomputes the chain and names the first edited or removed row and prints the head hash; `pa audit tail` lists rows; `pa audit check <tool>` shows what the policy would say. An unreachable database is logged, not an error: a deny is still a deny
details.Where it runs: inside the jarvisd generation: the MCP server, chat permission answers, factory approve and the CLI. The termhub front is still its own process (D25). Only voice and dashboard approvals look up a job's delivery; other channels are audited with what the request names. Passkey step-up stays off until PA_PASSKEYS=on

components.name: Supervisor (zero-downtime)
components.role: Owns the dashboard port and proxies it (HTTP, SSE, WebSocket) to the current worker generation, so a deploy starts the new worker beside the old one, switches without a gap and can switch back (plan items Z1, Z4).

where.work: the compiled jarvisd's supervise role (4.4), started by windows\pa-launch.ps1 from the pa-worker task (non-elevated since 2026-11-08), on 127.0.0.1:7300; generations on 127.0.0.1:<OS-assigned>
where.personal: the compiled jarvisd's supervise role, exec'd by linux/pa-launch.sh from the pa-worker unit, on 127.0.0.1:7300; generations on 127.0.0.1:<OS-assigned>

Ports: public: 127.0.0.1:PA_DISPATCH_PORT (7300), held by the supervisor for its whole life
each worker generation: 127.0.0.1 on a port the OS assigns (port 0), reported over IPC ({type: 'listening', port})
details.Roll: spawn generation N+1 (PA_SUPERVISED=1) → wait for GET /healthz ready (180 s at most) → route new requests to it → send N drain (N hands its passes over, Z2) → end N's SSE and WebSocket streams (clients reconnect, with Last-Event-ID, to N+1) → wait for N's in-flight requests (30 s at most) → keep N drained as the standby for 150 s (covers the drain and the deploy's 60 s watch), then stop it
details.Failed roll: a generation that exits or is not ready in time is killed; N keeps serving and the roll answers ok: false
details.Crash: the serving generation exiting on its own is replaced by the standby if one is held, else by a new one, backing off 1 s to 60 s
details.Control: one JSON line on a local socket: \\.\pipe\pa-supervisor-<port> on Windows, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pa-supervisor-<port>.sock elsewhere; {"cmd":"roll"|"rollback", "owner"?}, {"cmd":"lock"|"unlock", "owner"} or {"cmd":"status"} (status carries source, a hash of the running supervisor file); `node src/supervisor roll|rollback|status`; SIGHUP rolls on Linux
details.Background passes: single owner (Z2, src/util/lease.ts): every timer, watcher and the durable worker is declared on the scheduler (src/util/scheduler.ts) and runs only while its generation holds the lease (a row of the lease table on SQLite; pg_advisory_lock(7300) on the Postgres backend) on a dedicated connection. On drain the old generation stops its schedulers and releases the lease at once; the new one polls every 500 ms and takes over within a second. Each pass run also holds its own lock (another lease row on SQLite; pg_advisory_lock(7301, hashtext(name)) on Postgres), so a pass the old generation is still finishing is skipped by the new one until it ends; every other pass moves over at once. Undrain (rollback) takes the lease and the passes back
details.Rule: node builtins only; never loads worker code, so a deploy never needs to restart it
details.Rollback: {"cmd":"rollback"}: drain the serving generation, undrain the standby, wait for its /healthz (30 s), flip back, stop the other. Only while a standby is held (150 s after a roll)
details.Deploy (Z4): windows/redeploy.ps1, linux/redeploy.sh (run by termhub's Update after its pull, or by hand with -Pull/--pull and -DryRun/--dry-run) → node src/supervisor/deploy.ts: npm install when the package files changed, npm run build when one exists (none yet), roll, then /healthz + /api/version every 2 s for 60 s; 3 failed probes in a row, or not the new commit at the end → rollback, exit 1
details.Restart fallback: the scripts restart the task/unit (stop, end the supervisor and its generations (node, bun, or the compiled jarvisd), start, wait up to 120 s for the new commit) only when deploy.js exits 3 (no supervisor answers: the bootstrap) or 4 (src/supervisor/index.ts changed), or when they just rewrote a task/unit that still named src/worker.ts
details.Bootstrap: node src/worker.ts not started by the supervisor (an older task or unit, which a non-elevated deploy cannot rewrite) becomes the supervisor before loading any worker code; PA_NO_SUPERVISOR=1 runs the bare worker
details.Log: <state dir>/logs/supervisor.log (PA_DATA_DIR, else %LOCALAPPDATA%\personal-assistant or ~/.local/share/personal-assistant; PA_SUPERVISOR_LOG overrides): the supervisor's lines and each generation's stdout/stderr as [gen N], rotated at 5 MB, 3 kept. Workers log 'event loop blocked' for any stall over 1 s
details.Readiness: a generation says ready only at the end of its startup (passes declared, lease requested), not when its port opens: the module loading in between blocked the loop for seconds right after the flip
details.Deploy test (Z6): node src/e2e/deployTest.ts: during real rolls, 4 loops of GET /api/version, an /api/events stream reconnecting with Last-Event-ID while events are produced, and a termhub terminal printing ticks; passes only with zero failed requests, every event exactly once in order with no resync, and the terminal socket held with no tick missing. Spare mode (a supervisor on a free port, test/fixtures/deployWorker.js, a throwaway termhub) runs in test/deployTest.test.js; --live [--deploy] runs it against the stack (events through the store's wake-up (the SQLite outbox poll on these stacks, pg_notify on Postgres) and pa_event_seq)
details.Priority: the worker runs at Normal; everything it starts is lowered to Below Normal as it spawns (src/util/childPriority.ts). A below-normal worker got no CPU while other work filled every core and stalled up to 173 s
details.Keep-alive: the worker dashboard keeps idle sockets 65 s; the supervisor resends a GET that meets ECONNRESET on a reused socket. status and a timed-out drain list what is in flight (method, path, age)
details.Deploy lock: one deploy at a time: deploy.js holds <state dir>/deploy.lock (owner pid) and the supervisor's lock ({"cmd":"lock","owner","ttlMs"}, 15 min, released by {"cmd":"unlock"}) through the roll and the health watch; meanwhile any other roll, rollback or lock is refused naming the holder (deploy.js exit 5), and a roll during a roll is refused, not merged. The supervisor's crash respawn is not a deploy and ignores it
details.jarvisd (4.4): strict TypeScript (src/supervisor/index.ts; index.js a shim). The compiled jarvisd runs it: `jarvisd supervise` owns the port, its generations are `jarvisd generation`; the executable for each new generation is PA_JARVISD_EXE, else `current` beside the binary (written by a deploy that built jarvisd-<commit> next to it), else itself. status.runtime says node, bun or jarvisd; status.source is embedded at build. Tested with the compiled binary on Windows and Linux CI (test/supervisorBinary.test.js, deployTest --binary). Both stacks run jarvisd supervise (status.runtime jarvisd) since 2026-11-08
details.Launcher (4.4): the pa-worker task runs windows/pa-launch.ps1 and the unit linux/pa-launch.sh; on every start they read PA_RUNTIME: node (default) or bun start node src/supervisor, jarvisd starts the executable jarvisd/dist/current names as `supervise` (no Node), falling back to Node when none is built. deploy.js treats PA_RUNTIME differing from the running supervisor as a switch (restart); for jarvisd every roll and restart builds jarvisd-<commit> first. Switch or roll back: one setting, then redeploy (JARVISD.md runbook)

details.Waiting for your yes: a card at the top of the board, on Build and in Ask's Text mode (permission.client.js) for the PA chat's pending action prompt, with Approve / Deny through POST /api/chat/permission; src/chat/permission.ts reads the session's screen before one keystroke (Enter on Yes, or Esc). A factory job parked on an approval (needs_human) says "waiting for your approval" on Build and in Plan's Agent runs, each with Approve (POST /api/factory/jobs/<id>/approve); by voice, Jarvis's factory_approve
details.Live feed (plan 0.4, E3): GET /api/events: one SSE stream per page (events.client.js) of {id, topic, at, payload} with topics board, run, factory, routine and resync. On SQLite (both stacks) there is no NOTIFY: after a commit the worker reads new event_outbox rows onto the bus (another process's event arrives within 100 ms). On the optional Postgres backend, triggers (sql/034_events_notify.sql) NOTIFY pa_events on every change to commitment, proposal, draft, ledger_evidence, commitment_block, secret_request, notification, run, factory_board (only when its jobs change), routine and routine_run, from any process; one LISTEN connection per worker generation (src/events) feeds an in-memory bus with a 1000-event ring for Last-Event-ID replay. Outbox (plan 1.4, sql/036): the same trigger writes each event to event_outbox under its global number in the writer's transaction (3 days kept, pruned by the trigger every 1000th event), so a g<seq> Last-Event-ID the ring does not hold (a restart, another generation) is replayed from the table, and a LISTEN that reconnects backfills from it instead of resyncing; only a client more than 1000 events or 3 days behind, or a process-local id from another process, still gets a resync. SQL in src/repo/events.ts. Plan, Build and Routines refetch on it (the 30 s polls are gone; a 5 min fallback poll stays). Measured on the work laptop: row commit to SSE frame 2 ms p50, 11 ms max; Plan sees a change in about 0.5 s (its /api/state takes 0.4 to 0.6 s), Build in about 0.1 s. On SQLite (8.4.33) an event another process committed is read from the outbox within 100 ms, and /api/state builds in about 45 ms after such a write (it skips the reviews the page does not draw; sql-sqlite/010 indexes each source's newest fetched_at): was about 170 ms on a copy of the store. Across a roll (Z6): sql/035 numbers every NOTIFY from pa_event_seq, so both worker generations call an event g<seq>; a stream the supervisor moves to the next generation resumes from its Last-Event-ID instead of resyncing (src/events/bus.ts), because a generation starts listening before it says ready
details.Factory repos: Frozen with the factory (D30): Build's Repos section (src/dashboard/factoryApps.ts, factory.apps.client.js): the repos registered with the factory, each with its delivery and pipeline defaults and gate readiness (configured / not configured / missing tool), from the stored `app list` (no factory call per page load; refreshed behind the render). GET /api/factory/apps[?fresh=1], GET /api/factory/apps/<app> (`app show`: suggested gates, incl. ones mirrored from the repo's CI), POST /api/factory/apps (`app add`, X-PA) and POST /api/factory/apps/<app> (`app set --gate/--requires/--delivery-default/--pipeline-default`, X-PA). A gate is a command, none (the repo has no such check: skipped) or not configured; suggestions are prefilled for unconfigured gates and saved only on Save. App configs stay on the factory machine
details.Factory push: POST /api/factory/events (X-PA): a factory on this machine pushes {job_id, state, why?, updated_at?} or {jobs: [...]}; merged into factory_board at once (Build shows it in about 25 ms) and the full `job list` follows within PA_FACTORY_ACTIVE_POLL_SECONDS. A done, failed or cancelled job also settles the run that holds it right after the answer, through the factory pass's own apply on the stored job under the pushed state: run row ended, card moved and its context cleared, "Factory run #N" raised (17 ms in test/factoryPushSettle.test.js); a poll that read the run before the push writes nothing (the write is guarded on the status it read). The factory side is `factory serve` (E3): within 0.2-0.4 s of a story transition
details.Build board (plan 8.8.2): Frozen with the factory (D30): Build's default Board view (factory.board.client.js, /factory-board.js; List keeps the grouped list): a strip with active/idle, spend today and over 7 days on both runtimes (Claude Code's labelled notional, not billed) and runtimes paused at a provider limit with their resume time; a card per job with its progress (the TUI's handler ratio), the persona at work, state and why (paused, needs you), the EBS ETA (P50/P75/P95), PRs with CI and CodeRabbit, cost against its budget cap and a dot per step; a card unfolds its steps on one time axis, a lane per persona; a step opens the run viewer on the right: its turns (text, thinking, each tool call with arguments folded and its result, diffs, gates, usage, the end), streamed while it runs, with Open in termhub kept as a link. GET /api/factory/board (`factory job board`, cached 2 s, one read shared by a burst) and GET /api/factory/steps/<id>/events?cursor&limit&wait&at (`factory job step`, JOBS-API v1.11: cursor-paginated, `wait` long-polls up to 20 s on factory serve, `at` reads one record uncapped); src/dashboard/factoryBoard.ts checks every query value before it becomes an argv element. Re-read on the live feed's factory and run events, and every 10 s while a job is live and the page is seen (the snapshot moves with factory state the feed does not carry)
details.Passkey sessions (plan 7.1, PA_PASSKEYS=: Off: nothing changes (loopback Host, X-PA on POST, page tokens). On: once a passkey is registered, every request except /api/auth/*, /login, the theme, /healthz and /api/version needs the pa_session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, opaque, stored only as a SHA-256 in passkey_session; idle 30 min and sliding, 12 h hard ceiling). WebAuthn runs on @simplewebauthn/server (src/auth/ceremony.ts): single-use two-minute challenges, user verification required, 10 failed assertions a minute rate-limited. Step-up for high-risk approvals (merge, push to main, secret reveal; src/auth/stepup.ts): POST /api/auth/stepup/verify records a one-use, two-minute grant for exactly one approval id, whose challenge commits to that id; the dashboard demands it where auto_merge and push_to_main are accepted today (a dispatch card, a factory job, ids derived server-side), and the policy engine (4.3) calls hasStepUp() for the same kinds. Voice and MCP can never write a grant. The Plan card's approval prompt (permission.client.js) and Build's Approve (factory.client.js) show an 'Approve with passkey' button only after the server answers an approval with needsStepUp and an approvalId. Never locked out: the gate is open while no passkey exists, an unreadable store fails open, `pa passkeys reset` (interactive local terminal, type RESET) forgets every passkey and session, and PA_PASSKEYS=off is the other exit. Enabling it on the live stacks is pending the owner.
details.Build page (D30): Build (/factory, factory.html, build.board.client.js, src/dashboard/buildBoard.ts) is the Build agent board: GET /api/build?page=&limit= (ten runs a page: state, model, cost against its cap, tokens, result, branch, the agents' lanes with their last 40 tool calls, messages, needs_you, notional spend in 24 h), POST /api/build/runs {task, model, repo} (a run with no card), POST /api/build/<id>/stop|reply|send (X-PA). One card per run: a lane per agent (a bar pulses only while its agent works, an ended one is static; ticks are tool calls, red when one failed), tool-call steps, messages with a reply box on an open ask, Open in termhub and Stop. Polls every 5 s while an agent is live, 30 s otherwise. A debrief that finds nobody else in it (others_present false) discards the recording; `pa meeting solo` lists older ones, `--apply` removes them. Debriefing an episode again (it grew, or was re-matched to another calendar event) supersedes its older debriefs (meeting_debrief.superseded_by, sql/044): they stop showing, what they applied is adopted where the new one restates it and undone otherwise; `pa meeting supersede <old> <new>` does it by hand. `pa meeting import <file>` (and the dashboard's Import control in Recorded & past meetings, POST /api/debriefs/import with the file as the raw body, X-PA, up to PA_IMPORT_MAX_MB; GET /api/debriefs/imports for its progress) files a recording or .txt/.vtt/.srt transcript you were not in: ffmpeg (PA_FFMPEG) cuts audio and video into PA_IMPORT_CHUNK_SECONDS chunks, the faster-whisper server above transcribes each, and the text is stored as an audio_episode in state 'imported' on the loopback stream, tied to a calendar event (--event, else the one it overlaps, else --title), then debriefed. Live capture never continues, merges or supersedes an imported episode, and the model's others_present false never discards it

Each run's stream-json result carries total_cost_usd and usage; the PA's calls are recorded in llm_spend (backend cli) and the factory posts its runs there (backend claude_session). Usage since the pool's reset day against PA_CLAUDE_POOL_USD gives the credit left (src/claudePool.ts). Unset PA_CLAUDE_POOL_USD = not tracked.

Off, a spent pool is shown on Meter and runs carry on.

components.name: Golden-path check (pa e2e)
components.role: Plan E4: one command runs the golden path headless against the live stack (a dummy card to a draft PR on xvanov/dev-tools), times each hop, checks that every view links the same card, run, job, steps, sessions and PR, and cleans up.

where.work: `pa e2e [<workflow>]` in-process on the machine it runs on; `--on <machine>` runs it on another PA_MACHINES machine through its termhub (exec for --dry-run/--sweep, a session for a real run)

details.Path: card by commitments/request.js (as typed on the board), then the chat's factory_start tool (factory_continue with --branch; factory_resume with --resume), runtime claude_session by default or --runtime api --model m; delivery draft_pr. Each action tool goes through the user's approval path headless: the policy is asked about the call as the chat's hook asks it (it must answer ask), the prompt is answered on the policy channel e2e (actor pa-e2e, audited as an approve with subject <marker>:<tool>), then the call is audited on channel chat as the chat's MCP server audits it; the run checks both audit_log rows (view policy) and fails without them
details.Hops: card -> job started -> first session output -> PR opened -> CI done (+ step killed, job resumed with --resume), timed off `factory job status` polls (--poll, 10 s; every 1 s for up to 2 min while a start is due), woken early by run/factory events on the dashboard's GET /api/events (0.4); job started is the factory's own stamp where it has one (a research job's started_at, JOBS-API v1.5, else the first runs[].started_at), not the poll; each hop has a timeout (--timeout hop=seconds)
details.Checks: Plan GET /api/state and /api/commitments/:id (card.chain), Build GET /api/factory (paRun, stories, runs), Run termhub GET /api/sessions (links, alive or scrollback), MCP card and factory_job tools, GitHub `gh pr view` (head = story branch, draft) as the repo owner via GH_TOKEN from `gh auth token --user`; E2: an API step has a session whose scrollback shows a model turn
details.Cleanup: unless --keep: PR closed with --delete-branch, job cancelled if live, card dropped through the ledger, step and follow sessions killed (golden path, `pa e2e research` and `pa e2e review-fix`, which never closes its PR); `pa e2e --sweep` finds leftovers by the e2e-<uuid> marker on the card and the stored run, run_step and run_pr links, and cleans only cards no run may still own (a live job the factory has not updated for 90 min, a finished job or a jobless card after 15 min), so parallel runs do not cancel each other; `--sweep --marker e2e-<uuid>` cleans that one run now
details.Dry run: `pa e2e --dry-run`: database, factory configured and on this machine (D13), factory app for the repo and that something ticks it (JOBS-API v1.6 `ticked`), dashboard /healthz, /api/state, /api/factory, termhub /api/sessions, the chat tools, gh write access; creates nothing
details.Output: hop/timing table and a JSON report (--json alone; --report file); exit 1 on any missed hop or failed link
details.Workflows (8.2): `pa e2e <workflow> [--dry-run]` for each example below with an acceptance block (`pa e2e all --dry-run` for every dry run): whats-on (a TTS'd question replayed as the talk page does it: /api/talk/warm, the utterance's length, the 96 ms VAD wait, /api/talk/endpoint with /api/talk/transcribe, /api/talk/turn, /api/talk/tts at the first piece while the turn streams; end of speech to the first audio byte. Not measured headless: the VAD frame and the browser starting playback), research, build-pr and build-continue-pr (walked by hand on 2026-11-10 through POST /api/build/runs, D30; the pa e2e runners under these ids are still the frozen factory's driver and are not Build-aware yet), teams-ask (`--test-chat <id>`, a chat the store holds where only you wrote and only you are in it, your self chat by default; checked by the dry run too. It sends nothing: it prints a dated ask of yourself with a 46-character marker for you to type there, then follows that message: Teams' arrival stamp to raw.storedAt, the owed_by_me card's extracted_at, the card in GET /api/state after its board event, the new_ask notification's toasted_at; checks person, due and link; drops the card. `--timeout teams=600 ask=600`). `--on <machine>` runs any workflow there as the golden path does and brings its summary back (`--report`)
details.Evidence: <PA data dir>/e2e/<stamp>-<workflow>[-dry]/: summary.json (hops scored against the 8.1 acceptance block, cost against GET /api/workflow-limits' effective ceiling, links, checks, the rubric left for the 8.3 reviewer), transcripts/ (session scrollback, the fast-lane turn), report.md, screenshots/ of each view the acceptance block names except Ask, with the page's text beside each PNG, by a headless Chromium (PA_E2E_BROWSER, else Playwright's installed Chromium, Edge or Chrome; skipped with a note when none) driven over the DevTools protocol: shot once the page's own loaded signal holds (Plan/Build #updated past loading, Run termhub's open session) and the network is quiet, or after 20 s marked ready: false. Ask is a tool check in summary.json views.ask (method tool, the tool, an excerpt of its answer): chat for whats-on, factory_job for research and deepseek-pr, factory_continue for review-fix; headless /talk stays on Tap once to enable Jarvis, so it is not shot. teams-ask lists no ask view; the plain --screenshot (at load) is the fallback. Every shot ends by 60 s (each DevTools call has a deadline; at the shot's the browser is killed and the fallback skipped); a view not shot is a failed `evidence` check, never a skipped summary, and a run held on a promise nothing settles still writes summary.json and its --report at exit, non-zero

details.Migrations: plain numbered SQL in personal-assistant/sql, applied by src/db/migrate.ts at worker start
details.Repository layer (plan 1.2, 1.3): live: every SQL statement is in src/repo/<aggregate>.ts behind a named method (src/repo/sqlite/ holds the SQLite twins, PA_DB); code elsewhere calls repo.<aggregate>.<method>() and repo.withTx(). test/repoBoundary.test.js fails on SQL or a db/pg require anywhere else (POOL_ONLY names the few that hold a connection), test/repoCalls.test.js on a call to a method that does not exist. test/repoContract.test.js runs every method's contract (test/contract/*.contract.js) on a throwaway pa_test_* Postgres database and on SQLite
details.Expand/contract (Z3): a roll runs the previous generation on the new schema, so after 032 every migration is additive; drops, renames, retypes and tightened constraints ship later as a contract migration marked `-- contract: <expand file>`. test/migrations.test.js (src/db/migrationRules.ts) enforces it, refuses edits to applied migrations and checks the previous commit's INSERTs against the new schema without Postgres
details.Durable tasks: Absurd (vendored schema) for work that waits: chases, run reviews
details.Embeddings (audit 2026-11-07): text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims, embed once and never re-embed (plan D5). Embedded: message and document chunks (chunk), memory claims (claim), memory pages (memory_page), commitment text for semantic dedupe (commitment_vector). Never embedded: identifiers, statuses, board state, numbers, dates; PR and ticket refs dedupe by key (commitment anchors), not by vector. No call site embeds changing data or exact keys; stored vectors are 41.5k (31.1k chunks, 10.0k claims, 105 pages, 242 commitments) and re-embed only when their own text changes (a changed item body, a regenerated page) or when CONTEXT_VERSION is bumped, which is a decision, not a cleanup
details.Query embeddings: a search embeds its query once: normalized text (trimmed, whitespace collapsed, lower-cased) plus model and dimensions -> vector, in an in-memory LRU (PA_EMBED_CACHE_ENTRIES, 500) backed by query_embedding_cache (PA_EMBED_CACHE_ROWS, 5000 by last use); query time only, never ingest
details.Secrets: never here: the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager resource dev-tools/<stack>, Linux Secret Service service=dev-tools stack=<stack>; stack work on Windows, personal on Linux, PA_STACK overrides; entries from before the label under personal-assistant are still read) or the gitignored .env. `pa secrets migrate --from-env` (dry run by default, names only) moves the values the code reads back (config.secret(); the Anthropic and Azure keys through lazy config getters) and empties their .env lines. The software-factory reads its provider keys from the same keychain when .env leaves them unset (factory/keychain.py)
details.Backups: every 24 h, 14 kept (PA_BACKUP_DIR): pg_dump plus the factory state dir (logs and locks left out) plus a manifest of table row counts, in one tar encrypted with AES-256-GCM (src/backupCrypto.ts, pa-<stamp>.pabak). The key is the PA_BACKUP_KEY secret, generated into the OS keychain on the first backup (pa backup key init / export --to <file>); never beside the backups. A machine with no keychain still writes a plain .dump and says so. Restore drill: `pa backup restore --to <scratch db>` restores into a throwaway database, compares row counts with the manifest and drops it (needs CREATEDB and the vector/pg_trgm extensions). Since the 3.5 cutover both stacks back up their SQLite file instead (sqlite-store); its drill passed on both on 2026-11-08
details.Signed self-update: deploy.js --pull fetches, checks `git log %G?` on the fetched range against a trusted-signers file outside the repo (PA_ALLOWED_SIGNERS, default <data dir>/allowed_signers), then merges; with --from the same check refuses the roll. Until that file exists an unsigned commit only warns (--require-signed / PA_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1 refuse regardless). docs/native/SIGNED-UPDATES.md says how to enable signing
details.Id chain: plan E1: card -> run -> job -> step -> session -> PR as stored ids. run (commitment_id, factory_job_id, termhub_session_id, mr_url, external_id) plus run_pr (every PR of a run: number, state, CI) and run_step (every factory step: job, story, persona, termhub session id, machine, URL), written by the worker factory pass from job status (sql/033); read by the board (card.chain), the card detail, Build and the card / factory_job / sessions MCP tools

components.name: SQLite store
components.role: The store after phase 3 (plan D2): one SQLite file per stack (WAL, FTS5, vectors as float32 BLOBs, SQLCipher), behind the same repository layer as Postgres.

where.work: The store since the 3.5 cutover (2026-11-08): %LOCALAPPDATA%\personal-assistant\pa.sqlite, encrypted, PA_DB=sqlite in personal-assistant\.env, PA_SQLITE_KEY and PA_BACKUP_KEY in Windows Credential Manager
where.personal: The store since the 3.5 cutover (2026-11-08): ~/.local/share/personal-assistant/pa.sqlite, encrypted, PA_DB=sqlite, PA_SQLITE_KEY and PA_BACKUP_KEY in personal-assistant/.env (the Secret Service keyring is locked for headless processes there)

details.Backend (plan 3.1): src/db/sqlite.ts: better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers (optional dependency; N-API prebuilds for Windows and Linux) with src/db's interface. $n placeholders, Date/JSON/boolean encoding, and rows decoded by declared column type (timestamptz -> Date, jsonb and arrays -> JSON, boolean, vector -> Float32Array), so the SQLite repositories return what pg does. Writes and transactions take an in-process lock and BEGIN IMMEDIATE; plain reads use a second, read-only connection
details.Schema: sql-sqlite/*.sql, applied by src/db/sqlite.ts migrate() (src/db/migrate.ts hands over when PA_DB=sqlite): the same tables and columns as sql/001-038, tsvector columns as FTS5 tables (chunk_fts, chunk_fts_exact, claim_fts, memory_page_fts), the event triggers writing event_outbox under pa_event_seq, and `lease` for what were advisory locks
details.Repositories: src/repo/sqlite/<aggregate>.ts, the twin of each src/repo/<aggregate>.ts; createRepos() loads them when the backend says dialect sqlite. Every aggregate phase 1.2 has converted has its twin; each states where SQLite cannot say what Postgres says (FTS5 bm25 ranks, ASCII-only lower()/like, regexes tested in JS, millisecond timestamps), for the 3.4 shadow comparison
details.Contract (plan 3.2): test/repoContract.test.js runs every case on postgres and sqlite (a throwaway encrypted pa_test_* file, no server; CI runs it on Linux and Windows and fails if SQLite is skipped). Strict: a repository method without its SQLite twin fails (PA_CONTRACT_STRICT=0 reports todo for work in progress). Green on every aggregate of 1.2
details.Encryption: PA_SQLITE_KEY set: SQLCipher v4 (PRAGMA cipher=sqlcipher, legacy=4, key); the key lives in the OS vault or the gitignored .env
details.Health: The page's store dot is repo.system.ping() (the check's kind is postgres, which is that probe's name). It answers for whichever store PA_DB selects; on both stacks that is this file
details.Vectors: 1536 float32 per BLOB, copied from Postgres (D5: never re-embedded); exact scan with vec_distance_cosine (sqlite-vec, optional dependency; a JS fallback otherwise)
details.LISTEN/NOTIFY: no NOTIFY: after a commit the backend reads the new event_outbox rows and hands them to sessions (pool.connect()) that LISTENed, in-process only; other processes read event_outbox
details.Shadow comparison (plan 3.4): pa db compare --sqlite <file> (src/db/shadow.ts): eval questions and recorded searches through the same repository methods on Postgres (read only) and an export. Work stack 2026-11-08: board reads identical; vectors 0.98-1.0 overlap; SQLite hit@10 0.771 vs 0.625 and MRR 0.519 vs 0.413 on the eval gold items; nothing to recalibrate (rank fusion, reranker-scale abstain)
details.Vector search: two stages (sql-sqlite/007): sign bits per vector in chunk_bits / claim_bits ranked by Hamming distance, the best 400 re-ranked by exact cosine; 40-80 ms p50 over 31k chunks (an exact scan was ~530 ms; Postgres's approximate HNSW ~20 ms)
details.Pass reads (sql-sqlite/008): statements run on the event loop, and a chunk or claim row carries its 6 KB vector, an item its body and raw JSON, so a scan that tests one column reads the whole store. The passes' reads therefore go through narrow indexes (stale and unembedded chunks, unembedded claims, review counts, the reconciler's window, member-listing items), select ids before wide columns, and test text length from the record header (atLeastChars). A run of statements gives the loop a turn every 50 ms outside transactions (src/db/sqlite.ts). On the work store: 0.2-0.9 s per read before, 0-170 ms after; a worker rehearsal's /healthz stayed under 0.6 s. The spend per local day (sql-sqlite/009) reads a covering index and calls pa_local_day once per UTC quarter hour, not per row: 100-130 ms -> 45-60 ms over a week's 60k calls. The reconciler's dirty read (sql-sqlite/011) seeks source_item by fetched_at since the oldest check, instead of each ask's 30-day window
details.Keyword search: FTS5 (porter and exact indexes), Postgres's English stop words; items ranked on narrow columns, text read for the top rows only, each index's best 2,000 chunks when no filter applies. 61 ms p50 on the work stack (Postgres 0.9 s)
details.Cutover (3.5): docs/native/CUTOVER-SQLITE.md: rehearse (export + compare while running), stop writers, export, compare, PA_DB=sqlite in .env, start, verify (doctor, live feed, e2e, backup drill); the cutover's rollback was unsetting PA_DB while that Postgres still held the data. D24 retired those databases, so these stacks stay on the SQLite file. Done on both stacks 2026-11-08: personal (a near-empty store, seconds), then work (export 90 s, board reads identical, about 5 min down, restore drill PASS: 79 tables in 18 s)
details.Backups (3.5 prep): src/backupSqlite.ts, behind the same pa backup / pa backup restore --to / pa restore: VACUUM INTO snapshots on a read-only connection, on a worker thread like the bundle's encryption (consistent, compacted, still encrypted with PA_SQLITE_KEY): pa-latest.sqlite refreshed by the hourly backup pass when older than PA_SQLITE_SNAPSHOT_MINUTES (RPO), the nightly encrypted .pabak bundle with pa.sqlite and a manifest; the drill restores into a new scratch file and runs integrity_check, the FTS integrity checks, foreign_key_check, row counts and a search. Not Litestream: it cannot open a SQLCipher file and has no supported Windows build. Work stack size: 453 MB snapshot in 6 s, bundle 10 s, drill 10-12 s
details.Export (plan 3.3): pa db export --to sqlite <file> (src/db/export.ts): a read-only snapshot of Postgres into a new SQLite file, ids kept, vectors float for float (D5), Absurd's tasks into the SQLite queue, row counts and sampled vectors verified
details.Durable tasks (D19): Absurd is Postgres-only, so on SQLite the same tasks run on src/durable/sqliteQueue.ts: spawn once per key, step checkpoints, sleepFor, awaitEvent with timeout, retries with backoff, over sql-sqlite/006 (durable_task, durable_checkpoint, durable_event); a worker's claim on a task is a lease row. src/durable/index.js picks the engine by store

components.name: Build agent (one Claude Code agent per task)
components.role: Do opens ONE interactive Claude Code session in termhub on the claude.ai subscription: the card's own words (no composing model call) plus one editable agent prompt, given as the command's opening prompt (src/build/agent-prompt.md), in a fresh git worktree on a new branch when the card names a repo. The agent decides the task's kind (draft PR, markdown report, other), uses subagents for long work, never merges or pushes the default branch, and finishes with `pa run done`.

where.work: In-process in the PA worker and dashboard; the session is in this machine's termhub
where.personal: unknown: not set up yet

details.Run row: build_run (state starting|running|waiting|idle|done|failed|stopped, model, worktree, branch, termhub session, Claude session id, result, caps, idle_after_s, last_activity_at, activity JSON, cost, tokens, track JSON) and build_msg (note, ask, done from the agent; reply, send from Jarvis). Env JARVIS_RUN_ID tells the agent its run.
details.Model: haiku | sonnet | opus | fable per card (default sonnet), passed as claude --model (fable as its full id claude-fable-5-1; it has its own weekly limit); --session-id fixes the transcript path (~/.claude/projects/<cwd with non-alphanumerics as ->/<session>.jsonl).
details.Guards: a run whose session vanishes without `pa run done` is failed at once (with a notice); a live run over its cost cap (PA_BUILD_COST_CAP_USD, default $5, notional subscription dollars) or its wall-clock cap (PA_BUILD_WALL_CAP_MIN, default 120) is stopped: session killed, run stopped with the reason. Card-overridable (build.card.<id>). Worker pass build-runs, every 15 s.
details.Messaging: Agent to Jarvis: `pa run note "<text>"` (FYI), `pa run ask "<question>"` (blocks, polling its build_msg row, up to 30 min; prints the answer; the run is `waiting` and a notice says it needs you), `pa run done --result "<PR url | report path | one line>"`. The run id is $JARVIS_RUN_ID, set at launch. Jarvis to agent: `pa run reply <run> "<text>"` (answers the open ask), `pa run send <run> "<text>"` (typed into the live termhub session), `pa run stop <run>`; the chat has build_runs, build_run (reads) and build_start, build_set_idle, build_reply, build_send, build_stop (ask). Also pa run idle <run> <seconds> and pa run export [--since].
details.Subscription limits: src/build/usage.ts, GET /api/factory/usage (dashboard/factory.ts): the live 5-hour session %, weekly % and weekly Fable-scoped % with reset times, and extra-usage credits (cents to dollars), from Anthropic's undocumented GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with Claude Code's own OAuth token (claudeAiOauth.accessToken in ~/.claude/.credentials.json, re-read per fetch, never logged or returned; PA_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS overrides the path). Cached a minute (failures too); after each 429 in a row the wait doubles from 2 min to 30 min, serving the last good numbers marked stale (kept in <dataDir>/usage-last.json so a redeploy is not blind; PA_USAGE_CACHE overrides); any other failure or odd shape answers {ok:false, reason} and the Build panel shows limits unavailable. The Build board draws it as a Limits meter row (bars by severity, resets in 2h 10m; the Fable meter lit when Fable is the chosen model), refreshed every 20 s and on focus.
details.Tracking: src/build/track.ts reads the session transcript and its subagents (<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, with .meta.json) every 15 s: per agent tokens (in, out, cache read/write; usage deduped by message id), notional cost at API list prices (haiku $1/$5, sonnet $3/$15, opus $5/$25, fable $10/$50 per M tokens; cache read 0.1x, write 1.25x/2x), tool calls (name, short args, ok/err, ms). The view is build_run.track (JSON), the totals build_run.cost_usd/tokens_*. When a run ends the run is kept under <data>/build-runs/run-<id>/ (Claude Code prunes ~/.claude/projects after cleanupPeriodDays): the main transcript <session>.jsonl, <session>/subagents/, messages.json (the build_msg rows) and summary.json (run, card, task, model, repo, branch, state, result, error, started_at, ended_at, elapsed_s, tokens, cost_usd, agents, tool_calls by name, errors, messages); pa run export [--since <date>] prints every summary.json as JSONL.
details.Heartbeat: src/build/heartbeat.ts, worker pass build-heartbeat every 10 s, stat calls and one sessiond list call, no transcript parsing: last_activity_at is the newest of the transcript and subagent transcripts mtime, the termhub session being busy (PTY wrote in the last 1.5 s) and the run newest build_msg. Silent past the run own idle_after_s (default 240, PA_BUILD_IDLE_AFTER_S; set by build_start idle_after_s, the card menu, build_set_idle or pa run idle <run> <seconds>) while running: state idle, an urgent notice, and build_run.activity JSON {state, since, idle_s, last_tool, last_line} for Jarvis to decide from (build_run to look, build_send to nudge, build_set_idle, build_stop); it returns to running by itself on any sign of life. A run waiting on pa run ask is never idle. A session that vanished without pa run done fails the run at once with a notice. Idle runs are in build_runs.needs_you (kind idle) and the board Needs you.

examples.title: Start a PR with one Claude Code agent
examples.say: Do card 412 in dev-tools and open a draft PR.

steps.t: Wake word, VAD, transcription as above.
An action: the fast lane never answers it. It says 'On it.' and hands off your verbatim words.
Your words are typed into the PA chat through termhub. Claude Code reads card 412 (allowed) and calls build_start {card: 412, repo, model}.
build_start is on no allow list: Claude Code shows a permission prompt ("Start a Build agent on card 412 in dev-tools (haiku). Shall I?") and you say yes (or press Approve on the dashboard).

Build start (src/build/index.ts): a fresh git worktree on a new branch jarvis/<run>-<slug>, the card's own words plus the one agent prompt (src/build/agent-prompt.md) as claude's opening prompt, a build_run row; a fetch only when FETCH_HEAD is over 2 min old. The POST answers in about 3-5 s with a timings breakdown. An ended run's worktree is removed by the heartbeat (session gone, or 15 min after the end). Nothing metered, no factory (D30).
Opens ONE interactive claude --session-id session in termhub inside the worktree and types the brief into it. The agent edits, commits, pushes the branch and opens the draft PR itself with gh.
Runs on the claude.ai subscription: cost_usd is the notional API price of the transcript (read by src/build/track.ts), not a bill.
Branch pushed, draft PR opened, CI runs on it; the agent never merges.
`pa run done "<PR url>"` ends the run: state done, result = the PR URL, a durable summary at <data>/build-runs/run-<id>/summary.json. A session that vanishes without it is failed at once.
The build-heartbeat pass (every 10 s) flags a silent run idle after its idle_after_s; the Build board (/factory) and the Plan card chip show the run and its state.

acceptance.outcome: A draft PR is open on the repo from one Claude Code agent, never merged, and the run reports done with its URL.
